title: Activation-drift detector & adaptive calibration profiles for LLama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Asha Rao
description: Goal: Reduce accuracy regressions from FP8/INT8 quant profiles by introducing an activation-drift detector, model-specific outlier handling heuristics, and an adaptive layer-rescale calibration pass. This ticket implements a calibration guard that (1) detects runtime activation distribution drift relative to the calibration corpus, (2) applies a lightweight per-layer rescale or clamp policy for impacted layers, and (3) emits a pass/fail signal to the CI gating system for release of new quant profiles. Scope covers LLama-3, Mistral-7B/8x, and Qwen-family models used in the runtime model catalog.
background: We have seen intermittent generation quality regressions in customer workloads when switching to FP8 and INT8 runtime profiles. Root cause analysis points to: 1) rare but large activation outliers in certain attention/feedforward layers; 2) mismatch between calibration corpus and production prompts leading to activation distribution shift; 3) brittle global scaling heuristics that over- or under-scale activations. Existing tickets focused on static per-layer scaling and outlier clipping but lacked an automated detector and CI guard. This work combines detection, adaptive calibration, and CI validation.
acceptance_criteria: Activation-drift detector implemented and enabled in calibration harness
Adaptive layer-rescale policy that reduces per-token perplexity degradation to <= 0.7% vs FP16 baseline on heldout eval for each model family
CI gate that rejects quant profile artifacts if sample generation quality drops >1.5% on designated prompt suite
Automation report produced with histogram diffs, affected layers list, and applied scaling factors for each calibration run
Documentation and runbook updated with steps to re-run calibration and force-fallback to higher precision profiles
steps: Design detector: implement KL-divergence + peak-count metric across layer activations between calibration corpus and runtime sample set
Instrument harness: add lightweight collector during calibration to record per-layer activation histograms (buckets=256, exponential bins)
Heuristic rules: if KL>threshold or peak-count increases by >X, tag layer as 'drifted'
Adaptive rescale: for drifted layers run a local optimization to compute layer-scale in [0.5,2.0] that minimizes L2 error on quantized activations
Apply clamp: if rescale fails to reduce KL, apply a capped clamp on top percentile activations (top 0.1% -> clamp at 99.9th percentile)
Validation harness: run golden prompts (generation + eval metrics) comparing FP16, FP8, INT8 after adaptive calibration
CI integration: add a job that uploads calibration report and fails pipeline if quality thresholds are not met
Rollout plan: staged rollout for hosted catalog -> dedicated pools -> private, with automatic fallback to previous quant profile on failure
implementation_notes: Prototype used 1k diverse prompts sampled from telemetry and synthetic edge cases. Detector thresholds tuned on LLama-3 and Mistral-8x, conservative defaults chosen to avoid false positives. Adaptive rescale uses per-layer scale + bias-free re-centering to preserve attention dynamics. All telemetry buckets are anonymized and comply with PII policy. The calibration pass is synchronous but bounded to 30s per model to avoid blocking deploys; longer runs can be scheduled as async re-calibration.
experiments_and_results: LLama-3: baseline FP16 perplexity=18.4, FP8 after naive quantization perplexity=20.9 (+13.6%), FP8 with adaptive rescale perplexity=18.9 (+2.7%)
Mistral-8x: baseline FP16 ppl=22.0, INT8 naive ppl=26.8 (+21.8%), INT8 adaptive ppl=22.5 (+2.3%)
Qwen-7B: FP8 naive had generation hallucination rate +4% on factual QA suite; after clamp on 2 layers hallucination delta reduced to +0.6%
End-to-end CI runs: 50 calibration artifacts evaluated, 7 flagged by detector; of those, adaptive rescale resolved 5, 2 required human review and profile rollback
risks: Overfitting calibration to telemetry sample leading to missed edge-case drift
Added latency or deploy-time blocking if calibration run exceeds budget
False positives causing unnecessary rollback and churn in model catalog
mitigations: Keep detector conservative; allow opt-out via release flag for low-risk models
Run extended calibration asynchronously and expose results to ops dashboard
Add human review step for artifacts that resolve only with aggressive clamps
Throttle automatic rollbacks: require 2 failing CI runs or one human sign-off in production-sensitive customers
